answer: PoA resists Sybil strategies by binding every identity to bonded collateral and detecting coordinated equivocation: when k identities sign conflicting histories, their penalty scales as O(k^2), while detection imposes an exponential-in-k multiplier on aggregate capital loss through asymmetric depreciation. Consequently, a haven for hollow identities becomes a costly voyage from deposit to forfeiture, even when attackers rotate keys or distribute control.
